title: The New York Post Violates The New York Post's Community Guidelines.
subtitle: Absurdity, thy name is Murdoch.
body_html:
I penned a response the other day to the New York Post’s gross story. They were bashing OCD sufferers and every responsible organization thinks they suck. I dropped my article as a comment into the thread on the Post. I was informed of community guidelines for the New York Post comments section. I’d like recognize appropriate behavior, and start by saying: their community guidelines are acceptable.

Coming from the Post, it’s little like the NRA telling us about their sincere interest in gun safety, but credit where it’s due.

I could not help but notice, however, that the New York Post itself (and its business model of “Disgusting Exploitation of Human Misery as a Service” or DEoHMaaS) violates its own guidelines. It's a (plausible) violation of the community guidelines to post their own content!?!?

“Racist, sexist, homophobic, or other discriminatory comments” are not allowed. Oh my…It’s hard to defend their coverage choices. They are reporting on crucial stories about Trans-identified people as murderers because that’s news…that happened decades ago?

Share The Frontier Psychiatrists

I’m sure there is nothing discriminatory about this coverage of “whistleblowing” on clinics that follow the WPATH guidelines for gender affirming care?

And the pictures of a woman suffering from postpartum psychosis…after the horrific death of her children by someone who was deeply unwell. Not obscene…clearly…unless

Wait, let me check the dictionary like Amy Coney Barrett:

obscene

adjective

ob·​scene äb-ˈsēn  əb-

1: disgusting to the senses : REPULSIVE

2a: abhorrent to morality or virtuespecifically : designed to incite to lust or depravity … the dance often becomes flagrantly obscene and definitely provocative … —Margaret Mead

b: containing or being language regarded as taboo in polite usageobscene lyricsobscene literature

c: repulsive by reason of crass disregard of moral or ethical principlesan obscene misuse of power

d: so excessive as to be offensive

Enough already. Here is a helpful guide to help our media colleagues up their reporting game.

—Owen Scott Muir, M.D.

The Frontier Psychiatrists is a reader-supported publication, and also profits off of human suffering, but relieving it with edutainment.
